strings.research.baby.notes: The candidate was suggested by ChatGPT and confirmed by the user against the official map. Centre line only (162 m, a 17 m drop, 2709 to 2692), not an area boundary. It lies 78 m west-northwest of the upper Goodaura station and 129 m northwest of the bottom of Snow Park, like the green area on the map. In OSM it has no name and is tagged easy, not novice. The GPS around it is mostly slow movement in a station area (median 0.6 m/s), so it is no evidence for the name. There is no source for the position of the J-bar itself or for the area's boundary. The line is already shown on the site as an unnamed run. Medium confidence, thanks to the user's confirmation and the location.
strings.research.baby.partial: The centre line of the beginner area. The area's boundaries and the lift itself were not found in the data.
strings.research.bombora.notes: The candidate was suggested by ChatGPT and confirmed by the user against the official map. Centre line only (310 m, a 24 m drop, 2691 to 2667), not an area boundary. It starts 6 m from the lower Khada station and ends 43 m from the lower Kudebi station, like the green area on the map. An unresolved mismatch: according to skiresort the J-bar is at 2740 to 2780 m, and the way is 50 to 110 m lower than that. In OSM it has no name and is tagged easy, not novice. The GPS around it includes slow movement of lift queues. There is no source for the position of the J-bar itself or for the area's boundary. The line is already shown on the site as an unnamed run. Medium confidence, thanks to the user's confirmation and the location.
strings.research.bombora.partial: The centre line of the beginner area. The area's boundaries and the lift itself were not found in the data.
strings.research.firni_1.notes: On the official map Firni 1 is the eastern line of the Firni gondola. The only way in OSM, 668794719, runs on the eastern side of the gondola only in its top fifth (nodes 0 to 9, 692 m), and then crosses to the western side; so only the upper part is kept here, and the rest of the eastern line was not found. About Kobi: in OSM the way was called Kobi 1 in March 2023 and since March 2024 Frini, a misspelling of Firni (in the map's font Firni looks like Fimi). Kobi on the map is the name of the upper lift section, and the Kobi run (668794718) already has a separate line on the site above the upper Firni station. No GPS follows the line. ChatGPT kept the whole way as Firni 1 (medium); here it is split by the side of the gondola. The full way is attached as an alternative.
strings.research.firni_1.partial: Only the upper part was found, 692 m on the eastern side of the gondola. The rest was not found in any source.
strings.research.firni_2.notes: On the official map Firni 2 is the western line of the gondola: it leaves the upper part, descends on the western side, winds east near the lake and joins the gondola at the end. The lower part of way 668794719 (nodes 9 to 22, 1612 m) is on the western side and ends back near the gondola, like Firni 2, so it is kept here. The start of Firni 2 in the upper part was not found. OSM has no numbered name and there is no GPS, so the match is by position on the map only and confidence is low. ChatGPT marked it not-found. The full way is attached as an alternative.
strings.research.firni_2.partial: Only the lower part was found, 1.6 km on the western side of the gondola. The start in the upper part was not found.
strings.research.shino.notes: According to the legend of the official map, a dark blue dashed line is a Ski Way (a connecting route), so Shino is a link between areas and not a ski run; therefore its kind is ski-way, not run. On the map the line leaves the junction of Tatra 1 and Tatra 2 near the lower Shino station and continues east towards Zuma. The unnamed way 1259783832 (1283 m, descending from 2313 to 2182 m) matches this, but in OSM it was created on 10.3.2024 from a section that used to be part of Tatra 1 and has no name, so the match rests on the map alone and confidence is low. The western section of the dashed line (where the Shino label sits, towards Alpina) has no way in OSM. ChatGPT marked it not-found. The candidate 668794712 (230 m, connecting to the lower Shino station) remains as an alternative.
strings.research.shino.partial: The western section of the connecting route, towards Alpina, was not found in the data.
strings.research.soliko_2.notes: A partial section only: 372 m out of about 1,180 m (a third-party guide). The identification of the section is supported from three directions: in OSM its name is Soliko 2 with ref 2B (between 2A=Soliko 1 and 2C=Sportuli 1); its first node is shared with Soliko 1, and on the map Soliko 2 branches off Soliko 1; and it crosses the Shino lift at 2,424 m, about halfway along the lift, exactly as on the map. The rest down to the bottom of the mountain was not found in any source: of 11 GPS recordings that skied the start of the line, most continued along Soliko 1 or Sportuli 1 and not along a separate run, so no extension was made. ChatGPT marked exactly the same geometry high; mine is medium because it is partial. Way 1259783832 is not Soliko 2 (see Shino).
strings.research.soliko_2.partial: Only the top 372 metres out of about 1,180 m were found. The rest down to the bottom of the mountain was not found in any source.
strings.research.source_mta: The official MTA map (the image attached in the conversation), used only to identify name, colour, start, end and legend
strings.research.tatra_2.notes: An inner line from the upper station area to the lower Shino station (2282 m), including the lower trunk shared with Tatra 1. The geometry is two historical OSM ways that were both called Tatra 2 (668794706 and 1018641392), joined at a junction (42.4799,44.4818). This is the same geometry as in the ChatGPT package; in my earlier version the way ended at the junction only (1476 m). All 12 nodes of 1018641392 are also in the current Tatra 1, so the lower trunk is already drawn on the site under Tatra 1. The lower branch 668794711 (221 m) was called Tatra 2 in OSM between March 2023 and March 2024 and Tatra 1 since then, and it is attached as an alternative. The OSM names were reversed in 2019 (way 668794706 was then called Tatra 1), so the decision also rests on the map and on the user's confirmation.
strings.resort.soelden.sources: Lines: OpenStreetMap via OpenSkiMap, fetched {fetched}, as they are, nothing filled in. Colours follow the difficulty in the open map (easy blue, intermediate red, difficult black) and were checked against Sölden's official list of slopes. Horizontal lengths from the coordinates. Lift capacity and year built: Land Tirol (CC BY 4.0). Relief and altitudes: © offene Daten Österreichs – Digitales Geländemodell (DGM) Österreich (CC BY 3.0 AT), through the Terrain Tiles on AWS. Villages, roads, water and peaks: OSM. © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL.
